KR-LANG-001.reason_zh: 고추通常是辣椒，也能作为男性生殖器的委婉或儿童化说法。食物语境很正常，但在没有上下文的私聊里，큰 고추容易产生成人双关。
KR-LANG-001.reason_en: 고추 normally means pepper, but it can also be a euphemistic or childish word for male genitals. It is normal in food contexts, while 큰 고추 can sound suggestive in a context-free DM.
KR-LANG-001.cover_zh: 大辣椒还是男人的那里？

variants.zh: 큰 고추를 좋아해요.
variants.en: I like big peppers.

variants.zh: 先等等。你是在说做饭，对吧？
variants.en: Wait. You mean for cooking, right?

variants.zh: 不然呢？我今天在学食物。
variants.en: What else? I’m studying food today.

variants.zh: 고추是辣椒，但也能委婉指男人那里。
variants.en: 고추 means pepper, but it can also be a euphemism for a man’s private part.

variants.zh: 所以我刚刚像在宣布个人偏好？
variants.en: So I just sounded like I was announcing a preference?

variants.zh: 在没有食物语境的私信里，有一点ㅋㅋㅋ
variants.en: In a DM with no food context, a little ㅋㅋㅋ

variants.zh: 我的食物作业怎么突然这么危险。
variants.en: How did my food homework get this dangerous?

variants.zh: 고추 사진 좀 보내 줘.
variants.en: Send me a picture of a pepper.

variants.zh: 请在后面加上“做菜用的”ㅋㅋㅋ
variants.en: Please add “for cooking” to that ㅋㅋㅋ

variants.zh: 为什么？我只是想确认辣椒的大小。
variants.en: Why? I just want to check the size of the pepper.

variants.zh: 你每解释一次，听起来都更危险。
variants.en: Every explanation makes it sound more dangerous.

variants.zh: 等一下，고추还有别的意思？
variants.en: Wait, does 고추 have another meaning?

variants.zh: 有，但只有特定语境才会往成人方向理解。
variants.en: Yes, but it only gets the adult reading in certain contexts.

variants.zh: 好。我要的是超市版，不是限制级版。
variants.en: Okay. I want the grocery-store version, not the rated version.

KR-LANG-002.reason_zh: 커피是咖啡，코피是鼻血。两者并不完全同音，但初学者如果把元音说错，就可能把喝咖啡说成喝鼻血。
KR-LANG-002.reason_en: 커피 means coffee and 코피 means a nosebleed. They are not identical, but a learner who changes the vowel can accidentally say they drank a nosebleed.

variants.zh: 오늘 코피 마셨어.
variants.en: I drank a nosebleed today.

variants.zh: 你喝了什么？
variants.en: You drank what?

variants.zh: 咖啡啊。很正常。
variants.en: Coffee. Very normal.

variants.zh: 咖啡是커피。你刚说的是코피，鼻血。
variants.en: Coffee is 커피. You said 코피, a nosebleed.

variants.zh: 只差一个元音，早餐就变恐怖片了？
variants.en: One vowel turned breakfast into a horror movie?

variants.zh: 对。所以是커，不是코ㅋㅋㅋ
variants.en: Yes. So it’s 커, not 코 ㅋㅋㅋ

variants.zh: 我刚录了韩语日记：매일 코피를 마셔요.
variants.en: I recorded my Korean diary: 매일 코피를 마셔요.

variants.zh: 不要发布。
variants.en: Do not post that.

variants.zh: 为什么？每天喝咖啡很普通吧。
variants.en: Why? Drinking coffee every day is normal.

variants.zh: 你说的是“我每天喝鼻血”。
variants.en: You said, “I drink nosebleeds every day.”

variants.zh: 커피。커피。这样？
variants.en: 커피. 커피. Like this?

variants.zh: 现在是咖啡了。可以发了。
variants.en: Now it’s coffee. You can post it.

KR-LANG-003.reason_zh: 십팔是十八，씨발是冒犯性很强的脏话。两者并非同音，但辅音紧张度、元音或收音说不清时，初学者容易制造危险误听。
KR-LANG-003.reason_en: 십팔 means eighteen, while 씨발 is a very strong swear word. They are not identical, but unclear consonants, vowels, or final sounds can create a risky mishearing.

variants.zh: 听我的数数语音：열일곱, 씨발, 열아홉.
variants.en: Listen to my counting: 열일곱, 씨발, 열아홉.

variants.zh: 你从十七直接数到骂人了。
variants.en: You went from seventeen straight to swearing.

variants.zh: 我说的是十八！
variants.en: I said eighteen!

variants.zh: 十八是십팔。你刚才的开头太用力了。
variants.en: Eighteen is 십팔. Your opening sound was way too tense.

variants.zh: 所以我不是数错了，是直接骂人了？
variants.en: So I didn’t count wrong. I just started swearing?

variants.zh: 我还在。再数一次，慢一点ㅋㅋㅋ
variants.en: I’m still here. Count again, slowly ㅋㅋㅋ

variants.zh: 为什么我说십팔时，语音识别一直打出脏话？
variants.en: Why does speech recognition keep typing a swear when I say 십팔?

variants.zh: 因为你把两个词的发音混在一起了。
variants.en: Because you blended the pronunciation of two different words.

variants.zh: 但我只是想说房间号十八。
variants.en: I only wanted to say room eighteen.

variants.zh: 那就把십和팔分清楚，别把中间吞掉。
variants.en: Then keep 십 and 팔 clear. Don’t swallow the middle.

variants.zh: 韩语数字为什么自带危险模式？
variants.en: Why do Korean numbers have a danger mode?

variants.zh: 数字没有。你的发音有。
variants.en: The numbers don’t. Your pronunciation does.

KR-LANG-004.reason_zh: 니가是口语中常见的“你”加主格标记。英语母语者可能把声音误听成 N-word，但韩语原词没有种族含义。
KR-LANG-004.reason_en: 니가 is a common colloquial form of “you” with a subject marker. English speakers may mishear the sound as the N-word, but the Korean word has no racial meaning.

variants.zh: 니가 먼저 말했잖아.
variants.en: You said it first.

variants.zh: 等一下。你刚才说了英语里的那个禁词吗？
variants.en: Wait. Did you just say that forbidden word in English?

variants.zh: 没有。我说니가，就是“你”。
variants.en: No. I said 니가. It means “you.”

variants.zh: 我的英语耳朵刚刚拉响警报了。
variants.en: My English ears just set off an alarm.

variants.zh: 可以警觉，但别把韩语词当成英语骂人。
variants.en: You can be alert, but don’t treat a Korean word as an English slur.

variants.zh: 明白。今天的问题是我的耳朵，不是你。
variants.en: Got it. Today the problem is my ears, not you.

variants.zh: 韩剧字幕写“you”，但我听到的完全不是you。
variants.en: The drama subtitle says “you,” but I heard something very different.

variants.zh: 是不是니가？
variants.en: Was it 니가?

variants.zh: 对。我还以为演员突然在说英语脏话。
variants.en: Yes. I thought the actor suddenly used an English slur.

variants.zh: 不用处理。니가在韩语里只是“你”。
variants.en: Nothing to control. 니가 just means “you” in Korean.

variants.zh: 两个语言碰在一起，耳朵先误会了。
variants.en: Two languages collided and my ears misunderstood first.

variants.zh: 至少你先问了，没有直接取消整部剧ㅋㅋㅋ
variants.en: At least you asked before canceling the whole drama ㅋㅋㅋ

KR-LANG-005.meaning_zh: 非常强烈的韩语侮辱语。
KR-LANG-005.reason_zh: 部分英语母语者会把개새끼的连续音节听成“gay sexy”。这只是跨语言听感梗，不是翻译、词源或标准发音说明。
KR-LANG-005.reason_en: Some English speakers jokingly hear 개새끼 as “gay sexy.” That is only a cross-language mishearing, not a translation, origin, or standard pronunciation guide.

variants.zh: 韩剧里两个人打架，为什么突然有人说“gay sexy”？
variants.en: Two people were fighting in a drama. Why did someone suddenly say “gay sexy”?

variants.zh: 他没有。他说的是개새끼。
variants.en: He didn’t. He said 개새끼.

variants.zh: 那是什么意思？
variants.en: What does that mean?

variants.zh: 很重的骂人话。千万别当成可爱的英语谐音。
variants.en: It’s a strong insult. Do not treat the cute English mishearing as its meaning.

variants.zh: 我的耳朵把吵架听成了派对。
variants.en: My ears turned a fight into a party.

variants.zh: 字幕救了你。相信字幕这一次。
variants.en: The subtitles saved you. Trust them this time.

variants.zh: 我学到一个听起来像“gay sexy”的韩语词。
variants.en: I learned a Korean word that sounds like “gay sexy” to me.

variants.zh: 先别发语音。我大概知道是哪一个。
variants.en: Don’t send a voice note yet. I think I know which one.

variants.zh: 개새끼？
variants.en: 개새끼?

variants.zh: 对，而且那是很严重的侮辱语。
variants.en: Yes, and it is a very serious insult.

variants.zh: 所以它既不gay，也不sexy。
variants.en: So it is neither gay nor sexy.

variants.zh: 正确。只有你的英语耳朵很有创造力。
variants.en: Correct. Only your English ears are being creative.

KR-LANG-006.reason_zh: 在보지 마中，보지来自动词보다加语法形式-지，整句完全正常。只有把보지单独当名词时，它才可能是粗俗的女性生殖器说法。
KR-LANG-006.reason_en: In 보지 마, 보지 comes from the verb 보다 plus the grammar form -지, so the full phrase is completely normal. As a standalone noun, 보지 can be a vulgar word for female genitals.

variants.zh: 我发错截图了。보지 마.
variants.en: I sent the wrong screenshot. 보지 마.

variants.zh: 太晚了，而且我刚查了보지。
variants.en: Too late, and I just looked up 보지.

variants.zh: 你是不是把句子拆错了？
variants.en: Did you split the sentence wrong?

variants.zh: 词典给了我一个很不适合截图的话题。
variants.en: The dictionary gave me a topic that does not fit the screenshot.

variants.zh: 보지 마整体就是“别看”。这里不是那个名词。
variants.en: 보지 마 as a whole means “don’t look.” It is not that noun here.

variants.zh: 我不仅看了截图，还看了不该点的词典解释。
variants.en: I saw the screenshot and the dictionary entry I should not have opened.

variants.zh: 为什么“不要看”里面有一个成人词？
variants.en: Why does “don’t look” contain an adult word?

variants.zh: 因为你把보지 마从错误的位置切开了。
variants.en: Because you split 보지 마 in the wrong place.

variants.zh: 所以韩国人说这句时没有在开黄腔？
variants.en: So Koreans are not making an adult joke when they say it?

variants.zh: 完全没有。就是普通的“别看”。
variants.en: Not at all. It is simply “don’t look.”

variants.zh: 真正不该看的，是我刚才的搜索记录。
variants.en: The thing I should not look at is my recent search history.

variants.zh: 这次我同意。보지 마ㅋㅋㅋ
variants.en: This time I agree. 보지 마 ㅋㅋㅋ

KR-LANG-007.meaning_en: The metamorphosis process of a butterfly.
KR-LANG-007.reason_zh: 변태在生物学中可以表示变态或变态发育；日常用来称呼一个人时，通常是“变态、色狼”的侮辱性说法。
KR-LANG-007.reason_en: 변태 can mean metamorphosis in biology. In everyday speech, calling a person 변태 usually means “pervert” and is insulting.

variants.zh: 我的韩语课写着나비의 변태 과정。
variants.en: My Korean lesson says 나비의 변태 과정.

variants.zh: 为什么蝴蝶是变态？
variants.en: Why is the butterfly a pervert?

variants.zh: 在生物课里，변태是“变态发育”。
variants.en: In biology, 변태 means “metamorphosis.”

variants.zh: 那我可以叫你변태吗？你也会成长。
variants.en: Then can I call you 변태? You also grow.

variants.zh: 不可以。对人说通常就是“变态”。
variants.en: No. When you say it to a person, it usually means “pervert.”

variants.zh: 明白。只尊重蝴蝶的科学身份。
variants.en: Got it. I will respect the butterfly’s scientific identity only.

variants.zh: 词典说변태既是metamorphosis，也是pervert。
variants.en: The dictionary says 변태 is both metamorphosis and pervert.

variants.zh: 对，语境负责救场。
variants.en: Yes. Context does the rescue work.

variants.zh: 如果我只发“너 변태야”，还有科学可能吗？
variants.en: If I only text “너 변태야,” is there any scientific possibility?

variants.zh: 没有。那就是在骂我变态。
variants.en: No. That means you are calling me a pervert.

variants.zh: 好的，科学解释被你亲手关闭了。
variants.en: Okay. You personally closed the scientific interpretation.

variants.zh: 因为我不是毛毛虫。
variants.en: Because I am not a caterpillar.

KR-LANG-008.reason_zh: 在购物语境中，有明确商品宾语的이거 싸 주세요是正常表达。싸다也有排泄以及粗俗成人含义，所以把宾语和场景删掉后，单独发싸 주세요可能变得尴尬。
KR-LANG-008.reason_en: In a shopping context, 이거 싸 주세요 with a clear item means “please wrap this.” 싸다 can also refer to excretion and has a vulgar adult meaning, so removing the object and context can make 싸 주세요 awkward.
KR-LANG-008.cover_en: Wrap it or an adult request?

variants.zh: 语言软件教我说싸 주세요。
variants.en: My language app taught me to say 싸 주세요.

variants.zh: 它有没有先给你一个商品？
variants.en: Did it give you an item first?

variants.zh: 有一盒礼物。为什么？
variants.en: There was a gift box. Why?

variants.zh: 那이거 싸 주세요就是“请包起来”，很正常。
variants.en: Then 이거 싸 주세요 means “please wrap this,” and it is normal.

variants.zh: 如果我只发싸 주세요呢？
variants.en: What if I only text 싸 주세요?

variants.zh: 没有商品和场景，就可能出现非常不购物的理解。
variants.en: Without an item or context, it can get a very non-shopping interpretation.

variants.zh: 懂了。以后我把이거一起说。
variants.en: Got it. I’ll keep 이거 in the sentence.

variants.zh: 이거 싸 주세요. 这是“请打包”对吧？
variants.en: 이거 싸 주세요. That means “please wrap this,” right?

variants.zh: 对，在商店里拿着东西说就对。
variants.en: Yes, when you say it in a store while indicating an item.

variants.zh: 朋友说千万不要只说后面三个字。
variants.en: A friend said never say only the last three syllables.

variants.zh: 不是绝对不能说，是没有上下文会很怪。
variants.en: It is not absolutely forbidden. It just sounds strange without context.

variants.zh: 韩语：请携带商品使用。
variants.en: Korean: use only while carrying merchandise.

variants.zh: 这条安全提示我批准了ㅋㅋㅋ
variants.en: I approve that safety warning ㅋㅋㅋ

KR-LANG-009.meaning_en: Do you want an iced Americano?
KR-LANG-009.reason_zh: 아아是아이스 아메리카노的常见缩写，뜨아是뜨거운 아메리카노的缩写。아아同时很像连续发出“啊啊”的声音。
KR-LANG-009.reason_en: 아아 commonly abbreviates 아이스 아메리카노, while 뜨아 abbreviates 뜨거운 아메리카노. 아아 also looks like someone repeatedly saying “ah.”

variants.zh: 아아 마실래?
variants.en: Do you want an iced Americano?

variants.zh: 你为什么突然惨叫？
variants.en: Why did you suddenly scream?

variants.zh: 我没有惨叫。我在说冰美式。
variants.en: I didn’t scream. I said iced Americano.

variants.zh: 아아是咖啡？
variants.en: 아아 is coffee?

variants.zh: 对，아이스 아메리카노的缩写。
variants.en: Yes. It is short for 아이스 아메리카노.

variants.zh: 아아아아아아。
variants.en: 아아아아아아.

variants.zh: 你这是点六杯，还是需要帮助？
variants.en: Are you ordering six cups, or do you need help?

variants.zh: 我知道了。아아是冰的，뜨아是热的。
variants.en: I got it. 아아 is iced and 뜨아 is hot.

variants.zh: 今天学得很快。
variants.en: You are learning fast today.

variants.zh: 那如果我很累，可以发아아吗？
variants.en: Then if I’m exhausted, can I text 아아?

variants.zh: 可以，但我会先问你要咖啡还是救援。
variants.en: Yes, but I will ask whether you want coffee or rescue first.

variants.zh: 韩国聊天需要饮料识别系统。
variants.en: Korean chat needs a beverage detection system.

variants.zh: 早上八点前默认都是咖啡。
variants.en: Before 8 a.m., assume it is coffee.

KR-LIFE-001.meaning_en: Iced Americano even if I freeze to death.
KR-LIFE-001.reason_zh: 얼죽아来自얼어 죽어도 아이스 아메리카노，是韩国网络中形容天气再冷也坚持喝冰美式的常见缩写，但不代表每个韩国人都这样。
KR-LIFE-001.reason_en: 얼죽아 shortens 얼어 죽어도 아이스 아메리카노 and describes choosing iced Americano even in freezing weather. It is a popular meme, not a rule for every Korean.

variants.zh: 你那边零下八度，为什么动态里还是冰咖啡？
variants.en: It’s minus eight there. Why is your story still an iced coffee?

variants.zh: 얼죽아。
variants.en: 얼죽아.

variants.zh: 这是求救暗号吗？
variants.en: Is that a distress code?

variants.zh: 是“冻死也要喝冰美式”的缩写。
variants.en: It is short for “iced Americano even if I freeze to death.”

variants.zh: 你可以喝热的，不需要证明什么。
variants.en: You can drink it hot. You have nothing to prove.

variants.zh: 我不是在证明。我只是在保持人格一致。
variants.en: I’m not proving anything. I’m maintaining character consistency.

variants.zh: 今天很冷，但我还是얼죽아。
variants.en: It’s cold today, but I’m still 얼죽아.

variants.zh: 我查到了完整意思。你们对冰块太忠诚了。
variants.en: I found the full meaning. You are too loyal to ice.

variants.zh: 不是所有韩国人，只是我们这群人。
variants.en: Not every Korean. Just people like us.

variants.zh: 你说得像一个咖啡组织。
variants.en: You make it sound like a coffee organization.

variants.zh: 入会条件：冬天也不准改热饮。
variants.en: Membership rule: no switching to hot drinks in winter.

variants.zh: 我选择活着，先不申请。
variants.en: I choose life, so I will not apply yet.

KR-SOCIAL-001.meaning_zh: 我老公，字面形式是“我们老公”。
KR-SOCIAL-001.meaning_en: My husband, literally phrased as “our husband.”
KR-SOCIAL-001.reason_zh: 韩语常用우리指自己的家人、学校、公司甚至配偶，强调共同体归属。直译成英语时，容易让学习者误以为这个人是多人共享的。
KR-SOCIAL-001.reason_en: Korean commonly uses 우리 for one’s family, school, company, and even spouse to express group belonging. A literal English reading can make the person sound shared.
KR-SOCIAL-001.cover_zh: 我的老公还是我们的老公？

variants.zh: 我看到一个韩国博主写우리 남편。
variants.en: I saw a Korean creator write 우리 남편.

variants.zh: 为什么是“我们的老公”？还有谁？
variants.en: Why is it “our husband”? Who else is involved?

variants.zh: 没有别人ㅋㅋㅋ 韩语常用우리来称自己的家人。
variants.en: No one else ㅋㅋㅋ Korean often uses 우리 for one’s own family.

variants.zh: 所以우리 남편实际可以是“我老公”？
variants.en: So 우리 남편 can actually mean “my husband”?

variants.zh: 对。是共同体表达，不是共享账号。
variants.en: Yes. It expresses belonging, not a shared account.

variants.zh: 谢谢。韩剧家庭关系恢复正常了。
variants.en: Thank you. The drama’s family relationships are normal again.

variants.zh: 우리 엄마是“我们的妈妈”，对吗？
variants.en: 우리 엄마 means “our mom,” right?

variants.zh: 字面上像，但说话人通常是在说自己的妈妈。
variants.en: It looks literal, but the speaker is usually referring to their own mom.

variants.zh: 那우리 회사也是“我的公司”？
variants.en: Then 우리 회사 is also “my company”?

variants.zh: 更像“我们公司”。우리强调所属的群体。
variants.en: More like “our company.” 우리 emphasizes the group you belong to.

variants.zh: 韩语的“我们”工作量也太大了。
variants.en: Korean “we” is doing a lot of work.

variants.zh: 我们谢谢它。你也开始会用了。
variants.en: We thank it. You are already learning how to use it.

KR-SOCIAL-002.reason_zh: 밥 먹었어?字面确实是在问吃饭，但熟人之间也常用它表达关心或自然开启聊天。具体是在问饭还是问候，要看关系和上下文。
KR-SOCIAL-002.reason_en: 밥 먹었어? literally asks whether someone ate, but close friends also use it to show care or open a conversation. Whether it is literal or social depends on context.
KR-SOCIAL-002.cover_en: Asking about food or checking on you?

variants.zh: 밥 먹었어?
variants.en: Did you eat?

variants.zh: 吃了。三明治、苹果，还有半袋薯片。
variants.en: Yes. A sandwich, an apple, and half a bag of chips.

variants.zh: 我只是随口关心一下ㅋㅋㅋ
variants.en: I was just casually checking on you ㅋㅋㅋ

variants.zh: 你问了，我就提交完整报告。
variants.en: You asked, so I submitted the full report.

variants.zh: 韩国朋友之间，这句话也可以只是开启聊天。
variants.en: Among Korean friends, this can also simply open a conversation.

variants.zh: 明白。下次我只回答“吃了”，不交证据。
variants.en: Got it. Next time I’ll say “yes” without submitting evidence.

variants.zh: 你每天都问밥 먹었어? 你在统计我的饭吗？
variants.en: You ask 밥 먹었어? every day. Are you tracking my meals?

variants.zh: 没有，就是看看你有没有好好生活。
variants.en: No. I’m just checking whether you are taking care of yourself.

variants.zh: 所以它有点像“你还好吗”？
variants.en: So it is a little like “are you doing okay”?

variants.zh: 有时候是，但也可能真的在问你吃没吃。
variants.en: Sometimes, but it can also literally ask whether you ate.

variants.zh: 韩语连关心都先检查碳水。
variants.en: Even Korean care checks your carbs first.

variants.zh: 你还有力气吐槽，看来吃过了。
variants.en: You still have energy to tease me, so I guess you ate.

KR-MEME-001.meaning_zh: “你思想开放吗？”的韩式英语模仿说法。
KR-MEME-001.meaning_en: A parodied Korean-English way of saying “Are you open-minded?”
KR-MEME-001.reason_zh: 这句话因Hongdae Guy网络角色走红，用来讽刺在弘大向外国女性搭讪的特定男性类型。它是网络模仿与安全争议中的梗，不代表所有韩国男性。
KR-MEME-001.reason_en: The phrase went viral through the Hongdae Guy character, parodying a specific type of man approaching foreign women in Hongdae. It is a meme tied to safety debates, not a description of all Korean men.
KR-MEME-001.cover_zh: 普通英语还是弘大搭讪暗号？
KR-MEME-001.cover_en: Normal English or a Hongdae pickup line?

variants.zh: 为什么评论区都在刷“Are you open mindeu?”
variants.en: Why is everyone commenting “Are you open mindeu?”

variants.zh: 你刷到Hongdae Guy了？
variants.en: Did you find the Hongdae Guy meme?

variants.zh: 对。我还以为大家突然开始练英语。
variants.en: Yes. I thought everyone suddenly started practicing English.

variants.zh: 那是在模仿一种对外国女生搭讪的男人。
variants.en: It parodies a type of man who approaches foreign women.

variants.zh: 所以这句现在自带警报声？
variants.en: So the line now comes with an alarm sound?

variants.zh: 在这个梗里，是的。但别拿它代表所有韩国男人。
variants.en: Inside this meme, yes. But don’t use it to represent every Korean man.

variants.zh: Are you open mindeu?
variants.en: Are you open mindeu?

variants.zh: 你为什么突然变成Hongdae Guy？
variants.en: Why did you suddenly become Hongdae Guy?

variants.zh: 我只是练英语。虽然这本来就是英语。
variants.en: I’m just practicing English, even though this is already English.

variants.zh: 现在它是一个很具体的网络梗，还带搭讪讽刺。
variants.en: Now it is a very specific meme with pickup-line satire attached.

variants.zh: 那我下一句是不是“Do you live alone?”
variants.en: Then is my next line “Do you live alone?”

variants.zh: 不是。你的下一句是“我停止模仿”。
variants.en: No. Your next line is “I will stop copying him.”

variants.zh: I stop mindeu.
variants.en: I stop mindeu.

KR-LANG-010.meaning_en: I have never had sexual relations.
KR-LANG-010.reason_zh: 관계可以是普通的关系、关联，但在恋爱或男女语境里，관계하다、관계를 가지다、관계한 적 없다常会往性关系理解。想表达“没谈过恋爱”，更自然是연애한 적 없어요。
KR-LANG-010.reason_en: 관계 can mean a general relationship or connection, but in dating or male-female contexts, 관계하다, 관계를 가지다, and 관계한 적 없다 often point to sexual relations. To say “I have never dated,” 연애한 적 없어요 is safer.

variants.zh: 我韩语日记写了：저는 관계한 적 없어요.
variants.en: I wrote in my Korean diary: 저는 관계한 적 없어요.

variants.zh: 你确定要写这个吗？
variants.en: Are you sure you want to write that?

variants.zh: 我想说我没谈过恋爱。
variants.en: I want to say I’ve never dated.

variants.zh: 那应该说연애한 적 없어요.
variants.en: Then say 연애한 적 없어요.

variants.zh: 관계不是relationship吗？
variants.en: Doesn’t 관계 mean relationship?

variants.zh: 是，但你那句更像在说没有性关系经验。
variants.en: Yes, but your sentence sounds more like no sexual experience.

variants.zh: 我的日记突然太私人了。
variants.en: My diary suddenly got way too private.

variants.zh: 관계这个词是不是很安全？
variants.en: Is 관계 a safe word?

variants.zh: 要看你把它放在哪里。
variants.en: It depends where you put it.

variants.zh: 比如우리 관계 좋아요?
variants.en: Like 우리 관계 좋아요?

variants.zh: 那是关系不错，正常。
variants.en: That means our relationship is good. Normal.

variants.zh: 那관계한 적 없어요呢？
variants.en: Then what about 관계한 적 없어요?

variants.zh: 那个就容易变成成人话题了ㅋㅋㅋ
variants.en: That one easily turns into an adult topic ㅋㅋㅋ

variants.zh: 韩语词典只给我一半真相。
variants.en: The Korean dictionary gave me only half the truth.

variants.zh: 所以你有我这个活人注释。
variants.en: That’s why you have me as a living footnote.
